assumptions: The founder uses only public knowledge and independently created assets, with no Reckitt confidential information, systems, documents, contacts, or relationships.
The initial target is an EU mid-market buyer with meaningful packaging complexity and no adequate existing specification-management workflow.
Regulatory interpretation is reviewed by qualified independent counsel rather than represented as automated legal advice.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots from several target buyers at the proposed price, measured audit-to-subscription conversion, fully loaded account economics and renewal, supplier response rates, executed data and processing rights, and proof that the workflow wins against low-cost tools and incumbent PLM alternatives.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: PPWR creates a genuine need to assemble packaging-type documentation and supplier evidence, and a SKU-linked record is better aligned to approval work than generic storage. The insight is weakened because established specification platforms and inexpensive PPWR tools already address much of the same workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Regulatory duties, buyer-side supplier-document activity, and public paid PPWR offers support real pain and budget availability. No target buyer has paid for or committed to this particular audit-plus-vault offer, and phased obligations make urgency uneven across portfolios.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid audits and annual subscriptions offer favorable cash conversion and potentially attractive software margins. However, the proposed pricing, audit-to-subscription conversion, onboarding burden, CAC, retention, specialist costs, and owner earnings are unvalidated, while low-price substitutes challenge both price and margin assumptions.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: EU mid-market brands and manufacturers lacking capable PLM systems form a plausible beachhead with identifiable budget owners and triggers. The segment is not quantified or narrowed by obligation, portfolio complexity, geography, or incumbent-system gap, so its economically accessible size remains uncertain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A lightweight supplier-evidence experience could win some underserved accounts, but low-cost specialists already offer overlapping repositories and supplier tools, while Specright demonstrates incumbent bundling. There is no exclusive channel, right, or proven niche in which the candidate can dominate.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful packaging record could extend across suppliers, SKUs, audits, adjacent EU requirements, and additional geographies. Expansion depends on first obtaining customer permissions and repeatable evidence collection, neither of which is established.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Schemas, accumulated records, and workflow switching costs could compound after adoption. Yet records remain customer- and supplier-controlled, benchmark rights are absent, access is nonexclusive and uncontracted, and competitors can reproduce the software functionality.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: SKU-level evidence organization and audit exports may improve convenience over spreadsheets. The evidence does not establish a material advantage over products priced from €29 monthly, a €999 annual supplier-linked repository, or an incumbent platform with approvals and automated PPWR reporting.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The regulation's general application from August 2026 creates a timely compliance window and active documentation work. Momentum is moderated because important substantive measures phase through 2030, producing variable near-term urgency.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Consultants, laboratories, and converters are plausible referral sources, but no referral or acquisition agreement is evidenced. The plan therefore relies on an unvalidated channel, with unknown sales cycle, conversion, CAC, and access to mid-market budget owners.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation skills, capital limit, and part-time availability fit a bounded test. Execution still requires supplier participation, customer data rights, regulatory counsel, security, insurance, and substantial onboarding, while strict separation from employer resources constrains domain access.

highest_value_structural_change: Replace dependence on a speculative shared data moat and unsigned referral channels with a direct-sold, prepaid, tightly scoped evidence-operations service whose customer agreement explicitly authorizes the request workflow and record retention.
main_structural_strength: A real regulation-driven supplier-document workflow can support a prepaid audit wedge and recurring SKU maintenance if the candidate becomes part of packaging approval.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed premium subscription lacks validated demand, economics, distribution, and rights, while direct low-price substitutes and incumbent bundling undermine differentiation.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PPWR Connect and PPWRify already offer overlapping declarations, supplier tools, repositories, and evidence trails at far lower prices, while Specright bundles supplier collaboration, approvals, and automated PPWR reporting.
